#1809. Frenkie De Jong hits back at critics and sends Hansi Flick message

By Naim Beneddra | 04 Nov 2026 19:44

Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong has expressed his frustration at the constant speculation surrounding him, while making it clear that he wants to reclaim a regular starting place under Hansi Flick.

The Netherlands international spoke out after reaching 300 appearances for the Catalan giants during Tuesday's 3-0 Champions League victory over Aston Villa, having recently returned from a lengthy injury absence.

De Jong believes that his performances, fitness and future attract considerably more scrutiny than those of his teammates, particularly when he is unavailable for selection.

However, the 29-year-old also delivered an encouraging update on his physical condition, insisting that his knee is no longer causing problems and that he is ready to compete for a more prominent role.

His comments arrive at an important moment for Flick, with Barcelona preparing to face Atletico Madrid this weekend and uncertainty emerging over the availability of fellow midfielder Rodri.

Speaking to reporters following the victory over Aston Villa, De Jong acknowledged that the speculation surrounding him had become a recurring source of frustration.

"There is always a bit of noise around me, especially when I'm not there," the midfielder said, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo.

"For some reason, in the summer when there is no football, or when I'm injured..."

De Jong went on to suggest that he receives more attention than other members of the Barcelona squad, although he accepted that this might partly reflect his personal perception.

"I feel that there is always more noise around me than around others. But perhaps that's just my impression when people talk about me. These are things I don't have much control over."

The Dutchman's remarks follow several months of questions about his fitness and position at Camp Nou.

De Jong sustained a knee ligament injury while representing the Netherlands at the 2026 World Cup, leaving him unavailable for the opening weeks of Barcelona's campaign.

During his recovery, he also addressed reports concerning his relationship with Flick and the club's hierarchy, rejecting suggestions that he had fallen out with the German coach.

His latest comments suggest that the scrutiny remains a sensitive subject, even after his return to competitive action.

Nevertheless, De Jong was keen to emphasise that his physical condition has improved considerably.

"I feel very good, very strong, with a lot of desire and motivation," he explained.

"My knee isn't bothering me. What's happened has happened."

The midfielder made his first appearance of the season as a substitute against Real Madrid on October 25, before starting Barcelona's emphatic 6-1 league victory over Alaves six days later.

Flick deployed him in central defence against Alaves, illustrating the versatility that has allowed the former Ajax player to operate in several positions during his Barcelona career.

Tuesday's Champions League encounter brought another significant moment, as De Jong replaced Pedri in the 70th minute to make his 300th competitive appearance for the club.

He was subsequently presented with a commemorative shirt by his teammates.

Having already surpassed Philip Cocu and Ronald Koeman, De Jong holds the record for the most competitive appearances by a Dutch player in Barcelona's history.

Despite his willingness to help in defence, De Jong made no secret of his preferred position or his desire to return to the starting lineup.

"I feel more comfortable in midfield, but I will help the team wherever it needs me," he said.

Asked whether he hoped to start against Atletico Madrid on Sunday, the Dutch international acknowledged that his recent injury would influence Flick's decision.

"I would like to start matches, but we have to take into account that I've been out for a long time, and that depends on the coaching staff."

His comments are particularly relevant following Rodri's withdrawal at half time against Aston Villa.

The former Manchester City midfielder complained of muscular discomfort during Tuesday's encounter, prompting Flick to introduce Marc Bernal for the second half.

Barcelona have since confirmed a minor hamstring injury, leaving Rodri's availability for the trip to Atletico in doubt.

Flick has already suggested that Bernal could be considered as a replacement, while also pointing out that De Jong has only recently returned from injury.

That leaves the Barcelona manager with a decision to make over his midfield combination, particularly given the demands of facing one of La Liga's strongest opponents away from home.

De Jong's ability to operate alongside Pedri, provide defensive cover or contribute further forward gives Flick another option, but his limited minutes this season remain a consideration.

The Dutchman has repeatedly expressed his commitment to Barcelona, having signed a contract extension until June 2029.

His immediate priority, however, is considerably more straightforward: putting his injury problems behind him and earning a place in the team through his performances.

After reaching 300 appearances, De Jong is determined that his next chapter at Barcelona should be defined by what he contributes on the pitch rather than the speculation surrounding him.

#1808. Mikel Arteta brands Arsenal stars ‘extremely far from our standards’ in Slavia Prague win

Mikel Arteta was not impressed with his Arsenal team in the second half of their 2-1 win at Slavia Prague on Wednesday, saying they were ‘extremely far from our standards’ after the interval.

The Gunners continued their unbeaten start to the Champions League group stage with victory in Czech Republic, with three wins and a draw from their opening four games.

Noni Madueke opened the scoring after just nine minutes and the Premier League champions had a two-goal lead by half-time thanks to Viktor Gyokeres.

Slavia Prague made things difficult for their high profile guests, though, producing 18 shots over the match and scoring a late consolation through Wiktor Novak.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Arteta praised the Czech side, who have picked up just one point from four matches, but accepted that the second half performance from his men left a lot to be desired.

‘First of all, you have to value the fact it’s very difficult to win away from home,’ Arteta told a post-match press conference. ‘We’ve done it against a very tough opponent, we expected that toughness.

‘Two very different halves – the first we played at a really high level in terms of intensity, tempo, quality and clarity in what we had to do, and what the game was demanding. We were very efficient – we should have scored three, four or five.

‘We didn’t make that gap, and at half-time, the message was clear. There was still a lot to do in the game – this was a team we were up against with huge spirit, and if you give them something, they will grab it.

‘Right from the beginning of the half, we were extremely far from our standards, the basics, the concepts, and everything we discussed to avoid. It was far from what we expect from each other, but we found a way to hold onto the result and win the game.’

‘I take full responsibility for the drop in the second half.’

Goalkeeper David Raya had a similar report to his manager and said Arsenal must improve as the campaign continues.

‘First half, we played really really well. We dominated the whole game, created a lot of chances and could have scored a few more goals,’ he said.

Midfielder Robbie Gotts has agreed a new contract committing him to until the summer of 2029.

Manager Grant McCann sees it as a coup for the League One club, who tied captain Owen Bailey down for another three years in the summer.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Gotts came through at Leeds United, but since moving to what is now called the Club Doncaster Sports Village from Barrow in 2025, he has carved out a role as a mainstay of the side alongside fellow midfielder Bailey.

"He epitomises everything we're about as a football club," said McCann. "He's hard working, energetic and someone who is always looking to improve.

“I'd like to thank Terry (Bramall, the club's owner) and Gavin (Baldwin, chief executive) for their support in making this happen.

"Robbie still had time remaining on his previous contract, but we're delighted to have secured his future for the longer term. It allows him to settle, enjoy his football and continue being an important part of what we're building here.

“He's been the heartbeat of the team over the last six or seven months and has continuously improved. The supporters love watching Gottsy play, and that's because he drives the mentality we want here. It's not just what he brings on the pitch, but the way he trains every day as well."

The 26-year-old, who joined Doncaster after four successful years at Barrow, took a little while to settle in the team last season but 44 appearances in all competitions, and Saturday's defeat at Milton Keynes Dons – when he came on as a half-time substitute – was the first league game he has not started this season.

He has impressed McCann off the field too.

“Robbie is like a sponge," he said. "You give him information and he absorbs it, takes it on board and goes out and delivers. He wants to learn, he wants to improve and he's always looking at ways to develop his game.

"He's got so many attributes we really like, and while there are still little things we want to add to his game, his energy, hard work, aggression and ability to look after the ball make him a fantastic player to work with.

“It's important that we reward people for their performances, and this is a real sign to the rest of the squad that if you come in and perform to a high standard, you'll be rewarded. We've worked hard to get ahead of the game with our contract planning, and this is another example of that.”

The desire to keep improving was high in Gotts’ mind when he talked about his new deal.

“Breaking into the team last season was a big moment for me and since then I've just wanted to keep improving and enjoying every match,” he said. “I've worked hard on my game, both on and off the pitch, and I feel like I've developed a lot since joining.

“I want to keep driving my own standards, getting better every day and helping the team as much as I can. We've got a great group of players and people at the club, and I genuinely believe we've got the togetherness and quality to push up the table.

“The supporters have been brilliant with me since I've been here, and it's always special to hear them singing my name. I want to keep giving everything for them and hopefully we can achieve some really good things together.”

#1806. Steve McManaman says he ‘feels sorry’ for two Arsenal stars

Steve McManaman said he ‘felt sorry’ for Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz following Arsenal’s 2-1 win over Slavia Prague as Mikel Arteta’s playing style means the forwards often ‘get the blame’ for the side’s more cautious performances.

Arsenal maintained their unbeaten record in this season’s Champions League as a pair of first-half strikes from Noni Madueke and Gyokeres proved decisive before Wiktor Nowak’s late consolation.

The result ensured the Gunners, last year’s runners-up, sit third four matches into their league-phase campaign following previous victories over Napoli and Lille and a 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich.

September’s 3-0 defeat at the hands of Brighton in the Premier League remains Arsenal’s only loss in all competitions this term, an impressive run that Arteta’s men will look to continue when they return to action at home to Hull this weekend.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Arteta made a total of six changes to his team that got the better of Liverpool on Sunday, with Gyokeres starting through the middle in place of Havertz at Prague’s Fortuna Arena.

The Sweden international has endured a tough start to the new season but played a key role in the opening goal, assisting Madueke with a hooked pass behind Slavia Prague’s defence for Arsenal’s breakthrough inside just nine minutes.

He then got on the scoresheet himself to double the visitors’ advantage shortly before the break, beating Nazar Domchak with a superb effort that went in off the upright.

While it proved a far more difficult second half for Gyokeres as Arsenal held firm to protect their lead, ex-Liverpool and Real Madrid star McManaman felt the striker should have come away proud with his night’s work.

However, the ex-England international expects Havertz to return to Arteta’s starting XI when the north Londoners return to top-flight action against Hull on Saturday.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I liked him in the first half. I think in the second half, when Arsenal became a little bit dishevelled, they weren’t as close to him so I think it’s hard,’ McManaman said of Gyokeres’ performance.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘When they are playing well, he is up there on his own. In the first half, they were very compact, they were very close to him, they were getting around the sides, they were making chances, so he looked dangerous.

‘In the second half, when it got really stretched and they were wide and he was up on his own, he looked as if he was just left alone a lot.

‘I think when Arsenal play as more of a unit, attacking and defending together, I think he looks better.’

Given Arsenal aren’t renowned for being the most ‘entertaining’ of teams, McManaman finds himself ‘feeling sorry’ for Gyokeres and Havertz in certain matches.

‘I do feel sorry for Arsenal forwards sometimes because they’re not an entertaining team, they’re not like a Barcelona. They defend very deep, they defend as a whole and it’s a long way to get to the other end of the pitch to score goals,’ he added.

‘They’re never going to be this entertaining, lovely, free-flowing side scoring goal after goal after goal, and then Gyokeres and Havertz sometimes get the blame because of that. It’s normally the midfielders and the defenders that we talk about.

‘But as I said, Gyokeres had a great first half, he did his best in the second half and he deserves what he got because he got an assist and he got a goal.’

Asked if it could be time for Arteta to trust Gyokeres with more minutes, McManaman replied: ‘Whenever a big game comes around, Arteta reverts to Havertz doesn’t he?

‘People keep saying that Havertz scores goals in the big games and he certainly did that against Liverpool so you can’t really contest that.

‘But I just think he trusts Havertz a little bit more. That’s all it is.

‘Gyokeres played against Slavia Prague and he did exactly what he needed to do. He had an impact on the game, he had a huge impact on the game and we’ll wait and see for Saturday.

‘But I always think that when big games come around, if it was a final or Arsenal or Manchester City, if both Gyokeres and Havertz are fit, then Arteta would always revert back to Havertz.’

Facing the media shortly after the final whistle, Arteta heaped praise on Gyokeres’ all-round display, applauding the Swede’s ‘connection’ with his team-mates.

The Arsenal head coach explained: ‘I thought he was really good. It was a game we believed would be really good for him, for the demands the opponent puts in and the spaces he could use.

‘He’s done it really well, not just for the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s really great news for him, because he really needed that performance.’

On Gyokeres’ combination play, Arteta added: ‘He did that really well, understood really well when to appear, when to threaten, because they leave people, they follow man-to-man in the midfield and leave spaces there.

‘So when I said he was really connected to the team, that was another example. I thought he had a great performance alongside the goal and assist.’

Asked whether not starting had been a challenge for Gyokeres, Arteta replied: ‘It’s a question for him, but I’d imagine every player wants to play every game, and Viktor is no different.

‘The players need to impact the game like he has done today when they get the opportunity, to show the level they can produce. It’s really positive for the team.’

Bukayo Saka is ‘a bit fragile’ and must work on preventing injury problems in future, reckons former Arsenal defender Mikael Silvestre.

The Gunners winger is currently sidelined with a hamstring problem picked up in a Champions League clash with Bayern Munich on October 21.

Saka is not expected to be back in action until December, with Noni Madueke filling in on the right flank in his absence.

Silvestre accepts that injuries are bound to occur for players of Saka’s ilk, but suggests he is not quite as robust as he could be.

‘When you are an explosive player like Saka, obviously the muscles are what will trouble you when you are doing those sprints all the time,’ Silvestre told PariuriX.com. ‘Maybe, he is a bit fragile, and with the amount of games things like this can happen.

‘What is important for him is the recovery and the prevention, because it’s very important for him that it doesn’t happen too often, because he is very important for Arsenal.’

‘But it’s important to get those wins against teams who are also potentially in the race, and to keep your distance from them.

‘The positives are the defensive side of things, the 3 points, and the fact that it was at Anfield. It breaks that negative dynamic but I think it’s just for the stats really.

‘I think you need your best players at the key moments featuring in the semi-finals and the final of competitions. Arsenal need to keep Timber fit, Saliba is coming back also. #1800. The Man Utd change Michael Carrick must make against Aston Villa to keep his job

With JJ Gabriel almost out the door at Old Trafford Manchester United, and Michael Carrick will now be tempted to pin all their hopes on another emerging star in Shea Lacey.

The 19-year-old has played himself into first-team contention after a dazzling display off the bench in Tuesday’s comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League.

While it was Bruno Fernandes’ penalty that sparked the revival and Matheus Cunha’s brace that got them over the line, Lacey’s fearless cameo on the right was the catalyst for change.

Even the perennially reserved Michael Carrick couldn’t hide his delight over the performance, noting the teenager has ‘that bit of mischief’ in his locker that troubled Roma for the final 15 minutes of the game. Lacey ended the contest playing in defence after Cunha’s red card with Carrick jokingly christening him his new right-back.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Lacey’s sharp, perfectly-weighted passing enabled United to get up the pitch with real intent – seldom seen this season. He completed every one of his attempted passes and completed all but one of his duels. Operating in tight spaces just in front of the touchline, his first touches and clever exchanges were on point from the moment he came on. His pass for Cunha’s winner couldn’t have been placed better.

It has been a long time coming for Lacey. Injuries shelved tentative plans for him to make his debut at 16 under Erik ten Hag in 2023 and it was a tough road back from those issues that threatened to halt his progress.

‘Everybody in the world knows about Shea Lacey,’ United’s former Under-21 manager Travis Binnion said last year. ‘So he needs a little bit of fortune, he needs to be patient with himself and everybody else needs to be really patient with him.’ That patience could now be about to pay off.

Whether Tuesday’s win was a turning point or another false dawn for United remains to be seen. Jose Mourinho and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer led United to delirium-inducing comeback victories over Newcastle United in Atalanta with identical scorelines when the pressure was mounting on their shoulders. Both were gone shortly after.

But with Carrick’s back against the wall, there is the opportunity to roll the dice with Lacey. The Liverpool-born talent thumped home a wonderful strike in the Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton but has seen just 31 minutes of action off the bench since. Excluding the second-half performance against Roma, United’s attack has lacked any verve or real invention. A change is needed and Lacey will feel this is his chance.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

It was on the right where he caused damage midweek with Amad Diallo making way for him after 75 minutes. It had been another disappointing evening for the Ivory Coast international who spurned huge opportunities against Chelsea four days earlier.

Since forcing his way back into the side under Erik ten Hag, Amad has been looked upon as United’s most naturally talented winger. But his goal and assist return has fallen woefully short of expectations. He is now approaching one year without a goal, last finding the back of the net in the 4-4 draw with Bournemouth on 15 December. In that time, he has provided two assists – one on the final day of last season against Brighton and the other for Joshua Zirkzee’s consolation goal in the 4-1 humiliation in Como two weeks ago.

His haul of 14 goals during his magnificent campaign with Sunderland in the 2022-23 season is a distant memory. A hat-trick against Southampton in January 2025 helped him to an impressive haul of 11 goals and 10 assists in his first full campaign back in Manchester but seven goal involvements in 40 appearances since the start of the 2025-26 campaign is not good enough.

Wayne Rooney alluded to Amad’s problem midweek and made his case for Lacey getting the nod.

‘Amad does some really good things, but it’s that end product, that is what takes you to the next level,’ he told Amazon Prime. ‘And the glimpses of what I’ve seen from Lacey when he has come on…he has got something in there, that little touch and little pass which United needed to get them over the line in this game.’

The win over Roma has shifted a few clouds amid the gloom hanging over Old Trafford and Sunday’s visit of Aston Villa now looks a more inviting environment for Carrick to make the change and put his faith in Lacey.

#1798. Chelsea's hidden gem: the 19-year-old nobody saw coming

By Naim Beneddra | 04 Nov 2026 20:21

The 19-year-old defender has been included in Graham Potter's squad for November's UEFA Nations League fixtures against Bosnia and Herzegovina and Poland, marking another important step in his development.

Antwi joined Chelsea's sister club Strasbourg on a season-long loan in August, seeking the regular first-team opportunities that had been difficult to obtain at Stamford Bridge.

His progress in Ligue 1 has been impressive, with the Swedish full-back starting eight of Strasbourg's nine league matches since arriving in France.

And his performances have not gone unnoticed by Potter, the former Chelsea manager, who revealed that he had also received positive feedback about the youngster from people associated with the London club.

Truppen till avgörandet i Nations League ? ??? Bosnien-Hercegovina Stockholm | 14 november ??? Polen Wroclaw | 17 nov https://t.co/PbV8lwkQZ3

Antwi is one of two uncapped players selected by Potter for Sweden's upcoming Nations League double-header, alongside Fiorentina forward Alieu Njie.

The defender's inclusion follows a series of encouraging performances in France, where he has quickly established himself in Hugo Oliveira's plans.

Potter explained that an injury to Bologna right-back Emil Holm had created an opportunity to assess Antwi at senior international level.

"Genesis has done well with the Under-21 national team too, and with Emil Holm injured, I've chosen Felix Beijmo as the more experienced option," Potter explained during Wednesday's squad announcement, as reported by Swedish outlet Fotbollskanalen.

"Then we have Genesis, with his qualities and his pace."

The former Brighton & Hove Albion boss also revealed that he had spoken to people familiar with Antwi's development at Chelsea.

"I've spoken to people I know at Chelsea, and they think highly of him," Potter added.

That assessment is particularly encouraging for the Blues, who have invested several years in the defender's development.

Born in Stockholm, Antwi moved to England when he was 11 and joined Chelsea's academy, progressing through the age groups at Cobham before earning his first senior opportunities.

He made his competitive debut for the London club against Copenhagen in the Conference League in March 2025 and subsequently featured against Djurgarden in the same competition.

Chelsea rewarded his progress with a new contract in September 2025, tying him to the club until 2028, with an option to extend the agreement for another two years.

However, the decision to send him to Strasbourg this summer has provided the youngster with a considerably greater level of senior experience.

Antwi initially featured at left-back in the French club's opening league defeat against Marseille before moving to the right side of the defence.

His versatility and athleticism have subsequently helped him retain a regular place in Oliveira's side, including appearances against high-profile opponents such as Paris Saint-Germain and Monaco.

Potter acknowledged the value of that experience, praising the youngster's development during his first extended spell in senior football.

According to the Swedish Football Association, the national team manager believes that Antwi's performances at such a young age make him an exciting prospect to assess during the international break.

Antwi's first senior international call-up represents a significant milestone for a player who had previously represented Sweden at youth level, including five appearances for the Under-21 side.

It also provides Chelsea with an encouraging example of how their partnership with Strasbourg can accelerate the development of promising academy players.

The French club recruited five players from Chelsea during the summer transfer window, although their experiences have varied considerably.

Antwi, goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen and midfielder Dario Essugo have all established themselves as regular contributors.

Jorgensen has started nine league matches, making 32 saves, while Essugo has contributed two goals and an assist in seven appearances.

By contrast, former Chelsea youngsters Deivid Washington and Omari Kellyman, who joined Strasbourg on permanent deals, have barely featured.

Washington has yet to make a competitive appearance this season, while Kellyman has played only six minutes.

Those differences underline the varied experiences of players arriving in France through the two clubs' shared ownership structure.

For Antwi, however, the move has already delivered an important personal breakthrough.

Sweden will host Bosnia and Herzegovina on November 14 before travelling to face Poland three days later, with Potter's side leading their Nations League group.

A victory against Bosnia would secure promotion to League A, giving the Chelsea youngster the opportunity to be involved in an important international occasion.

Antwi has not yet made his senior Sweden debut, but his selection provides recognition of the progress he has made since leaving Stamford Bridge in search of regular football.

For Chelsea, the next stage will be monitoring whether he can maintain that development throughout the remainder of his loan spell and return to London with a stronger case for first-team opportunities.

The idea was to demolish a large part of the San Siro, keeping standing only a south-east portion, around 30% of the external ramps. A piece of the Curva Sud would be preserved and a part of the orange stand, areas that will be used for new purposes.

#1793. Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer

Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.

The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the new City head coach, has landed his number one target.

City left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club. But a late move to replace the Argentine with Monaco midfielder Lamie Camara collapsed to the anger of the Premier League club, leaving Xabi Alonso one player light among his midfield options.

Having refused to meet Chelsea’s self-imposed deadline to sign Fernández for £120m earlier in the summer, City had to equal the £125m Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak 12 months earlier.

Fernández had made it clear that he wanted to leave Chelsea some time ago and was left out of Alonso’s squad for the victories last week over Luton Town, in the Carabao Cup, and Brighton.

Having initially wanted to join Real Madrid, Fernández set his heart on linking back up with Maresca at City. The pair share a close relationship and had kept in touch after Maresca left Chelsea at the start of the year.

This is the second time Fernández has become the most expensive player in British transfer history, having previously set the record when he joined Chelsea for £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window.

Introducing our new Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855

During his time at Chelsea, 25-year-old Fernández won the Club World Cup and the Europa Conference League but he was also at the centre of controversy.

In January 2025, Fernández posted a video of himself and some of his Argentina international team-mates singing an offensive song about France players of African origin after winning the Copa America. He apologised to his Chelsea team-mates and made a donation to an anti-discrimination charity, but was still made the team’s vice-captain.

Last season was Fernández’s best goalscoring campaign, as he netted 15 goals in all competitions for Chelsea but the club finished 10th in the Premier League table. In April, he was suspended for two games by the club for suggesting he would like to live in Madrid – which was perceived as a come and get me plea to Real Madrid.

He angered England fans with his celebration after scoring against Thomas Tuchel’s team in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final victory over England, before being sent-off in the final defeat by Spain.

Chelsea fans booed Fernández in pre-season, although the club’s travelling supporters sang his name when he was introduced as a substitute in the victory over Fulham at the start of this season.

Fernández thanked his team-mates and the Chelsea staff in an emotional farewell post on Instagram. He added: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

“Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

“Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

“I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

“But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

“But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.”

The sale of Fernández means that Chelsea have set a new British transfer record of their own, having secured more than £500m in sales and loan fees during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea set about spending some of the money made from the Fernández sale by agreeing a last-minute deal for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

Monaco had rejected a bid of £38.5m from Chelsea on deadline day, but an improved offer of £47m was accepted late on Tuesday night, only to be called off by Monaco on the stroke of the 11pm deadline.

Chelsea had been able to complete a medical during negotiations and Camara agreed to a six-year contract with the option of a further year to bolster Alonso’s midfield options, but he will now not join the club.

Chelsea had also seen at least one offer for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott rejected this summer, while the club showed an interest in Roma’s Manu Kone and explored whether or not a move for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi would be possible earlier this month.

In this scrupulously detailed account of Arsenal’s summer, Sam Dean assesses where things went right, and wrong, for the Premier League champions in the transfer market.

They have buttressed the two areas in which they were already strong by signing Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa, but failed to sign the level-raising forward Mikel Arteta coveted.

In fact, with Gabriel Jesus, Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli departing (as well as Ethan Nwaneri moving on loan), their weakest department is arguably weaker than this time last year. Christos Tzolis, signed for £34m from Club Brugge, is their only attacking purchase.

But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.

I want to thank every single one of you: the staff, the coaching team, the medical team, the physios, and everyone who works at Cobham and throughout this great institution.

To all my teammates over these years, thank you from the bottom of my heart for sharing so many moments with me. I was truly happy here, and I wish you nothing but the very best for the future.

Thank you for all the love and support you have given me and my family throughout these years. I will never forget it.

This group will give you many more reasons to be happy, and I will be happy for you too. Never doubt that.

You will always be in my heart, Blues. I will always wish you, always, nothing but the very best.

I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

Jack Grealish to Everton is done. A small gathering of fans are waiting outside Finch Farm, the club’s training base, but the calmness of this little road, will be at odds with the scrambling that is going on behind closed doors.

Crystal Palace have agreed a deal to re-sign Ben Chilwell. The 29-year-old was on loan at Palace last year and deal struck with Strasbourg for him to leave French club and return to the Premier League.

Sunderland were involved in the most bewildering transfer of the summer on deadline day as they fought a day-long tug-of-war with Crystal Palace for winger Malick Fofana.

On a day of claims and counterclaims, Sunderland have finally triumphed in the battle to land the Belgium international just an hour before the deadline.

But despite their success, it was a transfer that will leave a sour taste in the mouth to many, with the player repeatedly changing his mind about which club he wanted to join

As the saga dragged on, it is understood Fofana had a medical in Lyon with both Sunderland and Crystal Palace given access to the information as he still could not decide which club to join as talks continued into the evening.

Sunderland had a bid of around £25m accepted by Lyon on Tuesday morning and thought they had an agreement with both the player and his agent on personal terms and fees only for Palace to make a late attempt to hijack the deal.

The London club’s manager, Pierre Sage, who worked with Fofana at Lyon, is thought to have personally intervened in an attempt to persuade the player to move to South London. By late afternoon, Palace appeared to have got their man having also offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to the player and fees to his agency.

Sunderland, though, refused to concede defeat and, according to reports in France, launched a counter proposal of their own led by French owners Kyril Louis-Dreyfus who flew to Lyon to try and clinch the deal.

At one stage, it was even claimed that the player had two different private jets waiting at the airport to take him to either London or the North East depending on who he elected to sign for.

That was later refuted, although it is understood the player did have a medical in Lyon that could be viewed by both clubs before he made up his mind. That gave his representatives more time to thrash the terms of a deal with both clubs.

However, having failed to board an earlier flight to Lyon after talks with Palace advanced, Sunderland’s late push belatedly persuaded the 21-year-old to head to Wearside, and he is due to be unveiled on Wednesday morning.

Arsenal had also been linked with the player earlier this week but were not willing to match the asking price for Fofana who they viewed as a project player.

Mykhailo Mudryk’s loan move from Chelsea to Spurs has been confirmed.

Forgive the personal opinion but this is my favourite deal of the window. Mudryk played some of his best football under Roberto De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk. The Spurs head coach has even described Mudryk as “my son”, and has previously tipped him as a future Ballon d’Or winner.

After so long out of the game, Mudryk now has a coach who knows exactly how to get the best out of him. It might not work at all. Mudryk may need months to rediscover his match sharpness after so long out. But I am very excited to find out.

Iliman Ndiaye has been confirmed as a Manchester City signing. He moves on a five-year deal from Everton with the deal worth £65m.

The fee means Premier League spending has now surpassed the previous record for a summer window which stood at £3.14bn. The running tally now stands at £3.193bn.

Ndiaye says: “I’ve worked my whole life for an opportunity like this. City are one of the best clubs in the world and I’ve seen them win everything as I’ve grown up.

“To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I’m determined to grab it with both hands.

“It’s not always been easy in my career, but I always had the belief that I could play for a team challenging for the biggest prizes and now I’m here. It feels so good.

“I love to play with the ball on the floor in an attacking team that wants to score as many goals as possible. That’s why I know this is the perfect fit.

Chelsea had been holding off from sanctioning Enzo Fernández’s move to Manchester City while they searched for a new midfielder of their own.

But Chelsea ultimately felt they had no choice but to let Fernández, who made it clear he wanted to leave, go in the best interests of the club.

Chelsea believe they have a strong squad, regardless of whether or not a new player is signed today, and will continue to weigh up their options.

Chelsea have agreed a £125m package to sell Enzo Fernández to Manchester City so the saga is finally coming to a close.

Chelsea will be happy with a fee that equals the British transfer record and City head coach Enzo Maresca will be delighted to land his top target.

It feels like a win-win all round as Fernández wanted to leave Chelsea and the club wanted over £120m after their initial deadline to do a deal expired.

It remains to be seen if Chelsea land any of their three main deadline day targets with a few hours of the window to go.

Chelsea had a bid rejected for Lamine Camara, Roma have not been playing ball on Manu Kone and the identity of the mystery Premier League target has not yet emerged.

When Newcastle United’s recruitment team finalised their list of priority targets back in the spring Matías Fernández-Pardo featured prominently.

There was excitement about what he could bring to the team. There was a buzz of possibility. The 21-year-old forward had impressed everyone, from scouts to decision makers. The call to make him one of their first-choice targets, alongside Switzerland international Johan Manzambi, was unanimous. Just as it had been when Newcastle identified Alexander Isak as their leading target back in the summer of 2022.

These meetings are a place for ideas to be shared and different targets pushed. Everyone had their own opinion and various favourites, but Fernández-Pardo was, in the words of one member of Newcastle’s recruitment taskforce “the one”.

It is understood Southampton have been demanding that his salary be paid in full, which has scared off interested clubs in the second tier.

Chelsea will hold off sanctioning Enzo Fernández’s move to Manchester City until they are confident of making at least one signing of their own.

Telegraph Sport understands that Chelsea have already rejected one proposal from City for Fernández during club-to-club talks and are demanding a fee and payment terms that are favourable to them.

Chelsea also have three separate targets of their own as potential deadline signings – Lamine Camara, Manu Kone and one mystery target from the Premier League.

Monaco have already rejected a £38.5m bid from Chelsea for Camara. Roma manager Gian Piero Gasperini wants to keep Kone, although negotiations continue. And there is a third target from the Premier League, who is not believed to be Morgan Gibbs-White.

Chelsea must make significant progress on one of their targets before they will sanction Fernández’s sale – and City must make another bid that is more favourable to the club.

Monaco have rejected an opening €45m bid from Chelsea for midfielder Lamine Camara. It now remains to be seen if the club increase that offer.

Sunderland have been trying to sign a winger all summer and it appears that they have finally got their man in Lyon’s Malick Fofana.

Arsenal had been linked with a move for the 21-year old Belgium international.

Announcing Ansah! ✍️🔗 https://t.co/gweqxOt7aR pic.twitter.com/geZR60ZaTG

The Argentina forward missed three training sessions last week and was not included in Diego Simeone’s squad that travelled to Sevilla last weekend.

Nueva sesión de trabajo del Atleti en Majadahonda esta mañana. Julián Alvarez entrenando con normalidad con el resto del grupo. Objetivo, intentar estar en la lista de convocados para el partido ante el Athletic. Sorloth será baja por lesión. Imagen: @jsancris_ #ClubUria pic.twitter.com/IXAWX7mwrJ

Plenty of chatter about the future of Roma midfielder Manu Koné, who is linked with a move to Chelsea. The France international would be a strong acquisition for Xabi Alonso, but could his potential signing precede an Enzo Fernández exit? All will be revealed in due course...

Of Koné, former France manager Didier Deschamps said: “He’s very effective at winning the ball back, but he shouldn’t be limited to that role of defensive midfielder, because he also makes a difference in his use of the ball.”

Austria centre-back David Affengruber has emerged as potential deadline-day deal for Fulham as they look to bolster Alvaro Arbeloa’s defence.

The Elche player has been in La Liga for two years playing regularly and fits the data model at Craven Cottage.

Fulham are also trying deals for Real Madrid’s Manuel Angel and Eintracht Frankfurt’s Hugo Larsson as midfield options.

Sunderland are expected to complete the signing of centre-back Kevin Danso from Tottenham Hotspur with the player travelling to Wearside last night for the first part of his medical.

The Austria international will initially join on loan with an obligation to make the move permanent for £25m next year.

Danso had made it clear he wanted to leave Tottenham this summer in search of regular first-team football.

Eintracht Frankfurt are in talks with Nottingham Forest over another loan move for forward Arnaud Kalimuendo.

Frankfurt signed the Frenchman on loan in January and are negotiating a return for Forest’s £26m signing from Rennes.

Oliver Glasner, Forest’s head coach, had been intent on keeping Kalimuendo but it is understood Frankfurt’s strong interest has altered the club’s thinking.

Morato, the centre-back, is expected to join West Ham United on loan.

Forest are exploring potential signings but are determined to stay calm and only pursue deals that make financial sense. A winger and a No 6 are the two priority targets if there are deals to be done.

On Tuesday evening, the Tottenham and Brazil forward posted an emotional message on Instagram amid reports of a possible move back to Everton.

He wrote: “After everything I’ve been through in recent years, I decided that never again would others decide my future for me.

“I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I’ve been through worse, believe me!

“I have always made it clear at every opportunity that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it... just as I didn’t accept it when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.”

Richarlison added: “I stayed and gave my all. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

“If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I will return to the club of my heart. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy.

“But negotiations were being done the way other people wanted, and it won’t be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I will remain at the club’s disposal.”

It will be good news for Arsenal if Folarin Balogun completes his £40m move to Everton today. When Arsenal sold Balogun to Monaco in 2023, they negotiated a sell-on clause of 17.5 per cent. According to my maths, that means Arsenal will get £7m from this transfer. Not to be sniffed at!

Hull City are close to agreeing a fee of around £7.5m for Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas.

The Wales international has been a long-term target for Hull and negotiations are now approaching a conclusion.

Thomas has been pushing a move through and is expected to leave Stoke after one full season.

As has become the norm this summer Acun Ilicali has posted a cryptic message on X, which has prompted speculation among Hull City fans. The club has been linked with Everton holding midfielder Tim Iroegbunam.

Will Barcola hit the ground running at Anfield? The France winger registered 20 goal contributions in 49 games for Paris St-Germain last season.

A warm welcome from the skipper 😍 pic.twitter.com/95EAqUjYBn

The La Masia graduate secures a permanent move to Germany. Who knows how his career in England would have panned out had Chelsea not recalled him 25 days into his Sunderland loan at the beginning of last season...

Marc Guiu has completed a permanent transfer to Bundesliga side RB Leipzig. Everyone at Chelsea would like to thank Marc for his efforts during his time at the club and wish him every success as he begins the next chapter of his career with RB Leipzig.

What a couple of weeks it has been for Robert Sanchez. He came into this season as Chelsea’s No 1, but after a difficult start to the campaign and Emi Martinez’s arrival, reports suggest he could be moving away from Stamford Bridge on loan. Cesc Fabregas’s Como appears the probable destination.

Trevoh Chalobah, who left Chelsea for Como last month, has taken to his “secondary” Instagram account to post the following picture...

Meanwhile, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, striker flop Nick Woltemade is moving to Juventus on a season-long loan. The club’s record signing from as year ago at £64m is moving to Turin for a £3.5m loan fee with the Serie A squad covering the full cost of his wages.

Newcastle will complete the £51m signing of forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille today but that is expected to be it in terms of incomings.

The Belgium international will become the club’s eighth signing of the summer and his versatility – he can play as a centre forward, a No 10 or out wide – means there are no more gaps to fill in the squad.

In an ideal world, Newcastle would have liked to sign another defender but none of their targets were still on the market. With Dan Burn due to return from injury in a few weeks, they have four centre-backs while new arrival Amar Dedic can play on both sides as a full-back.

In terms of outgoings, Joe Willock and Jacob Murphy are expected to stay at the club despite interest from Nottingham Forest and Besiktas. Young striker Sean Neave will be allowed to leave on loan. The 19-year-old has offers from clubs in the Championship and League One but Newcastle want him to go somewhere he has the best chance of getting regular first-team football.

City have been this summer’s selling kings and have had six players leave the club in deals worth more than £45m. Compare that to the summer when Pep Guardiola first arrived at the club, in 2016, when City generated just £23m from sales and made losses on Edin Dzeko and Stevan Jovetic, while Martín Demichelis departed on a free transfer.

Fast forward to this summer and more than £300m worth of players have been sold, with a further £60m arriving at the end of the season when Omar Marmoush’s loan to Tottenham Hotspur becomes permanent.

Given how Jaissle wants Newcastle to play, it is plain to see why Fernandez-Pardo appeals to him. Quick, direct and only 21 – he would surely fit right in at St James’ Park.

A post shared by Ligue 1 McDonald's (@ligue1mcdonalds)

The Leeds wide man has a medical booked with Fiorentina today. He made a handful of appearances for Daniel Farke’s side during pre-season but has not featured since the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

✈️ L'arrivo di Gnonto a Firenze ⚜️ pic.twitter.com/nEFngsyxQP

Very unlikely that Liverpool will be doing any major incoming business but there may yet be some departures. Jayden Danns, who broke through three years ago and played in the 2024 League Cup final defeat of Chelsea, is attracting interest from clubs in Europe, who want to take him on loan. Danns, a promising striker, has had injury issues and is working his way back to full fitness but his long-term ambition is to prove to Andoni Iraola that he can be part of his squad.

Fax machines are whirring as the clock continues to tick towards the transfer deadline, but who does your club need to sign? Let us know in the comments below!

Aston Villa are to confirm the signings of £50m winger Ibrahim Mbaye and £25m centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis this morning.

Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis takes the number of Villa’s signings this summer to 10, with Unai Emery ruling out any more additions after the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal last night.

Emery also disclosed that forward Tammy Abraham will be staying at Villa Park, amid interest from Ipswich Town.

The one player who could leave today is Jamaica international Leon Bailey, who has interest from clubs in Europe, and Hull City.

Nottingham Forest can confirm Omari Hutchinson has joined AC Milan on a season-long loan deal, with the Italian club holding an option to make the transfer permanent.Everyone at Nottingham Forest wishes Omari all the best for his time in Italy. pic.twitter.com/fSv1uNGh2Y

Fulham remain locked in discussions with Rayo Vallecano to agree a fee for right-back Andrei Ratiu, with the Romania international having confirmed he wants to join Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. The spin-off with this deal is that it will accelerate Kenny Tete’s switch to Everton, for a fee in the region of £9.5m.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

Leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A big year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

#1792. Haaland: Man City need to step up better when in the lead

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Erling Haaland admitted Manchester City "need to step it up a bit" after twice letting a lead slip against RB Leipzig before eventually winning 3-2 in the Champions League.

City almost let three points slip out of their grasp, having twice taken the lead at Red Bull Arena, first through a Castello Lukeba own goal and then via Enzo Fernandez.

Ridle Baku and Antonio Nusa cancelled out the respective advantages, but Haaland popped up in the 78th minute to secure all three points, with both sides also hitting the woodwork from late chances.

Against no side have City won more games in major European competitions than they have against Leipzig (five).

But Haaland, who had just 18 touches, conceded the game could have ended much differently if City had taken their chances after they first took the lead in the 37th minute.

"Not sure how many touches I had, not the most, but what is the most important is that I managed to help the team to win," he told TNT Sports.

"I think we need to step up a bit, when we were 1-0 up, I think we needed to go at it, go for the second goal and then the third – that's what we have to do. We have to work on that.

"Keeping the ball, when to keep it, when to go, working together offensively and defensively. You can always be better, and there's always a new chance. A new game in three days, so that's lovely."

Three hard-fought #UCL points! 2-3 https://t.co/zSUD2USV0y

— Manchester City (@ManCity) November 4, 2026

Haaland enjoys playing against Leipzig, having netted 13 goals in nine appearances against them in all competitions.

It is his most against any opponent in his career in Europe's big five leagues.

"I think it is the most I have scored against a club," Haaland said about his record against Leipzig.

"I have played so many times against them in the Champions League with City and Borussia Dortmund too. Leipzig is a good team, so I am happy."

Leipzig have lost 10 of their last 12 Champions League matches (W2). Among sides with 10+ games in the competition since 2024-25, only Slovan Bratislava (100% – 12/12) have a higher loss rate than them (83%).

Despite only accumulating 0.9 expected goals (xG) to City's 2.2, Leipzig edged the shot count 14 to 12, with six of those on target (City managed five).

"That's football. I think, in my personal opinion, we deserved more than a point," Leipzig head coach Martin Demichelis, who represented City as a player, said.

"We produced an outstanding performance against the team currently second in the Premier League, a team that will probably fight for titles until the very end.

"I believe we produced our best performance without the ball, and we were also brave going forward with the ball, creating plenty of chances.

"I know that three points from four games isn't enough. But the way we played, that's exactly what this team needs to show in every game.

"It was very bitter. It's a very sad moment for the players, but I simply congratulated the players. That's the way forward."

#1791. AEK Athens 2-3 Real Madrid: Struggling Vinicius Junior puts in another alarming performance for Los Blancos

By Matt Law | 04 Nov 2026 21:07, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 21:09

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho said that he was pleased with Vinicius Junior's performance in Wednesday's 3-2 win over AEK Athens in the Champions League.

Vinicius has not played in La Liga for almost a month, having been sent off in the team's contest with Villarreal at Bernabeu on October 10.

The Brazil international was again absent against Racing de Santander on Sunday, but he was brought back into the XI against AEK in the league stage of the Champions League.

Vinicius again found it difficult to make his mark and was replaced in the 81st minute of the contest, three minutes after Kylian Mbappe had made it 2-2.

Mourinho praised Vinicius after the match, telling reporters: "Vinicius Junior did very well, from my point of view, he put in a good performance. Later, of course, I preferred to inject fresh blood into the flanks by making two substitutions."

However, the numbers behind Vinicius' performance paint a different picture.

According to Sofascore, Vinicius lost possession on 11 occasions, while he only had 48 touches during his time on the field against the Greek club.

Vinicius managed three shots but was unable to hit the target, while only one of his three crosses in the Champions League fixture was accurate.

The defensive numbers behind Vinicius' performance are also alarming, having failed to provide a single defensive contribution, while he was dribbled past twice and only managed to win two his seven ground duels against AEK.

Vinicius has scored just once in 12 appearances for Real Madrid this season, in addition to coming up with three assists.

There had been a host of speculation surrounding Vinicius' future over the summer, with Arsenal making a strong play to sign the 26-year-old.

However, Vinicius ultimately signed a new long-term contract at Bernabeu.

The forward has scored 129 goals and registered 103 assists in 387 matches for Real Madrid during a highly-successful period, but there is no question that the South American is currently struggling for form at Bernabeu.

#1790. Fenerbahce 3-2 Liverpool: Reds stunned in Istanbul to lose perfect Champions League record

Even Liverpool’s multi-million pound bench could not rescue a team floundering in Istanbul as a chaotic performance was punished by Fenerbahce as they twice came from behind to win 3-2.

Alexander Isak had scored within three minutes of coming on to put the visitors ahead going into the final quarter but, like in the first half, the lead lasted just four minutes before former West Brom trainee Archie Brown equalised courtesy of some lax defending.

But worse was to follow as Vedat Muriqi outjumped three players to nod in the winner and end Liverpool’s 100 per cent record.

And while Andoni Iraola will be scrutinised for making five changes, including resting three of his front four in Sunday’s defeat to Arsenal, it was the way the team lost their cool and control in a game they had in hand which was more damaging.

It was a harsh result on 19-year-old Trey Nyoni, who belied his relative inexperience with a composed performance capped by an excellent volley to open the scoring, becoming Liverpool’s youngest player to register his maiden goal in the Champions League and second-youngest scorer in the competition after Trent Alexander-Arnold.

But Liverpool’s Turkish troubles continued – they lost twice to Galatasaray last season – on a typically fractious night in Istanbul, with former Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood scoring the first equaliser with a free-kick which deflected in off Jeremy Jacquet.

Slavia Prague vs Arsenal: Champions League build-up - LIVE

Arsenal XI vs Slavia Prague: Starting lineup and confirmed team news

They had been in total command up to that point but from there the game descended into something more manic, which suited a team hammered 6-0 at Villa Park last month and stoked a febrile home crowd.

Many of Liverpool’s players did not cope well in that atmosphere but, to his immense credit, Nyoni shone.

Iraola’s choice to leave out Isak, Florian Wirtz and Cody Gakpo as they come to the end of a run of nine games in 27 days was understandable but it left his side toothless.

Bradley Barcola was deployed as striker but his unfamiliarity with the role was evident after failing to properly anticipate Joe Gomez’s low cross to the near post.

He did flick one header wide but struggled with the physicality of Fenerbahce’s centre-backs, even though Kojo Oppong was making his first Champions League start.

There was a lot of naivety within the visitors’ ranks – Victor Munoz snatched at an early chance when he was found in acres of space before redeeming himself by eventually forcing Ederson into a save – but none of it came from Nyoni.

The teenager was composed on just his seventh Champions League appearance – with everything going through him at the base of midfield.

His use of the ball, tactical awareness and unshakeable belief in his own ability meant amid the hurly burly of a typically Turkish clash he was head and shoulders above everyone else.

Many of Liverpool’s players did not cope well in that atmosphere but, to his immense credit, Nyoni shone.

Even the usually unflappable Virgil van Dijk’s patience was tested, pushing Irfan Kahveci to the floor at a second-half corner, having twice had Romelu Lukaku leave something on him in the early stages.

When Liverpool’s breakthrough came it was fully deserved as Rio Ngumoha’s cross to the far post saw Van Dijk’s pressure force Brown to head weakly to the edge of the penalty area where Nyoni dispatched the dropping ball via a deflection off Oppong.

But after a sliding Kahveci smashed against the crossbar from five yards, Greenwood’s free-kick went through the wall.

Isak headed in Gakpo’s cross with his first chance after those two and Wirtz were summoned in the 66th minute, but the unmarked Brown tapped in the equaliser and more poor defending saw Muriqi head home the winner.

#1789. GdS: Milan enjoying the ‘best ever’ version of Rabiot – renewal imminent as figures emerge

Adrien Rabiot continues to dazzle with his performances and goal contributions, which AC Milan intend to reward him for.

La Gazzetta dello Sport confirm that the discussions between Rabiot and Milan have been underway for some time regarding an ‘update’ to the terms of his contract. Gerry Cardinale has very clear ideas about his priorities, and the Frenchman is next on the list.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In recent months, several players have ascended to the fourth floor of Casa Milan to sign extensions. There have been the young talents (Camarda and Comotto, 2031), veterans (Modric, 2027) and core pieces within the squad (Pavlovic, Pulisic, 2031).

Rabiot clearly belongs to the latter category (but also to a certain extent the same one as Modric) and has become the most urgent task to complete in terms of contracts.

The parties are in fact talking based on a shared desire to move forward together. For Cardinale, Rabiot represents one of the pillars on which the team’s rebuilding will continue.

Rabiot is seen as a player with the wisdom of experience, a perfect example for the younger players, and someone with the qualities of a leader even without the captain’s armband. Milan want to get back to the top, by Cardinale’s admission, and they need players like Adrien to help the cause.

So, a contract extension until 2030 has been ready for him for some time now (his current one expires in 2028). After the summer Napoli rumours, Rabiot remained at Milan partly because of his existing deal, but also partly because Cardinale convinced him.

What happens now? The next crucial step will be with his mother. Indeed, it is Mrs. Véronique who manages the former PSG midfielder’s interests, and a meeting will take place shortly. A pay rise from €3.5m net per season to €5m per year – what Pulisic earns – seems reasonable to presume.

With Rabiot on nine goal contributions for the season (five goals, four assists) he needs just one more to match his total from the entirety of 2025-26. So, he seems to be ageing like a fine French wine. All that’s needed is a final push on the contract front to continue an undoubtedly happy marriage.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

#1786. "Lost his spark..." - Vinicius Jr handed brutal verdict by Spanish media despite Real Madrid win

By Lewis Blain | 04 Nov 2026 21:32

Real Madrid maintained their perfect start in the 2026-27 Champions League league phase with a 3-2 victory over AEK Athens on Wednesday evening, but Vinicius Junior failed to take advantage of an opportunity to impress Jose Mourinho.

The Brazilian was handed a chance to strengthen his claims for a regular starting position ahead of his return from domestic suspension, but delivered another underwhelming performance on a night where Yan Diomande continued to enhance his reputation.

Vinicius's display attracted widespread criticism in Spain, with one publication awarding him just 2/10, while several prominent journalists questioned whether he deserves to remain in Madrid's strongest starting XI.

ElDesmarque were particularly scathing, awarding Vinicius just 2/10 and criticising his lack of attacking influence and defensive contribution. They highlighted his failure to track back, the space he left behind him and the fact that he completed none of his attempted dribbles.

AS were similarly unimpressed, describing his first half as ineffective and his second-half efforts as "un quiero y no puedo" - 'trying but unable to deliver'.

Former Real Madrid player and coach Jorge Valdano felt that "La palabra aceptable no es para un jugador como Vinicius" - 'the word acceptable does not apply to a player like Vinicius' - adding that he had produced just one good attacking move.

AS deputy editor Tomas Roncero was even more direct, declaring "Vini tenía una opción para lucirse, pero nada" - Vini had an opportunity to shine, but 'delivered nothing'. He subsequently questioned whether the Brazilian deserved to start, claiming that he had "perdido la luz" - 'lost his spark'.

Cadena SER's Dani Garrido agreed that Vinicius had wasted his opportunity, while Real Madrid correspondent Javier Herraez offered a pointed comparison with his rival for a starting position: "Diomande es un ejemplo, aprende de él Vini" - 'Diomande is an example, learn from him, Vini.'

The growing statistical gap between Vinicius and Diomande makes the criticism particularly difficult to dismiss.

According to figures highlighted by El Pais, Vinicius has attempted 37 dribbles this season, successfully completing just 15 at a rate of 40%. Diomande, meanwhile, has attempted 56 and completed 36, boasting a considerably better success rate of 64%.

Even more concerning is that Vinicius has gone two consecutive Champions League matches without attempting a single dribble, an extraordinary statistic for someone whose explosive running and ability to beat defenders have traditionally been his biggest strengths.

Diomande is therefore offering Mourinho an increasingly convincing alternative, with AS suggesting that the summer signing is already several lengths ahead in the battle for a starting position.

One disappointing performance would not normally threaten the status of a player with Vinicius's achievements, but the mounting criticism suggests that his problems are becoming a recurring issue rather than an isolated loss of form.

The Brazilian still possesses the quality to turn things around, but he needs to rediscover his confidence, directness and defensive commitment sooner rather than later.

With Diomande making a compelling case to remain in the team, Vinicius can no longer rely solely on his reputation to guarantee a starting position at the Bernabeu.

#1785. Cardiff 3-3 West Ham: Scott Parker oversees incredible fightback in first game in charge

Scott Parker saw his West Ham side recover from three goals down to draw 3-3 at Cardiff in a thrilling first game in charge.

Jack Moylan’s first hat-trick in English football had Cardiff in cruise control at half-time and Hammers fans venting their anger.

But the Hammers – inspired by captain Jarrod Bowen – fought back in incredible fashion as Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman netted to secure a point.

Parker was confirmed as Hammers boss on Wednesday morning – just 24 hours after Nuno Espirito Santo’s departure – but it was a tough watch for the former England midfielder initially as Moylan had Cardiff 3-0 ahead inside 39 minutes.

Moylan scored a hat-trick on his Republic of Ireland debut against Grenada in May, but this was his first club treble since scoring three for Shelbourne in May 2023.

The draw extends Cardiff’s unbeaten home league run to 10 games over the last two seasons, while West Ham occupy the final play-off place in eighth.
